report:
**Conclusion:** Current clinical evidence refutes the claim that taking ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 infection. Major health organisations and extensive research studies confirm that ibuprofen is safe to use for managing COVID-19 symptoms.

**Origins of the Claim:** 
In March 2020, French health authorities raised early concerns based on anecdotal reports suggesting that patients taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) experienced severe disease progression. Theoretical hypotheses also suggested NSAIDs might mask early infection symptoms or upregulate ACE2 receptors, the binding target for SARS-CoV-2.

**Scientific Evidence:**
Subsequent rigorous clinical trials, observational studies, and meta-analyses evaluated thousands of patients and found no connection between ibuprofen use and adverse COVID-19 outcomes:
* **No Adverse Risk:** Research demonstrates no association between NSAID use and increased risks of hospitalization, mechanical ventilation, or mortality in COVID-19 patients.
* **Regulatory Consensus:** Global regulatory bodies—including the World Health Organization (WHO), the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the European Medicines Agency (EMA)—evaluated the data and concluded there is no evidence that ibuprofen aggravates COVID-19. 

Patients can safely use ibuprofen or acetaminophen to treat fever and body aches associated with COVID-19 according to standard dosage guidelines.

**Sources:**
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
* Drug and Therapeutics Bulletin (BMJ): https://dtb.bmj.com/content/58/5/69
* PubMed Central: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7287029/
* The Lancet Rheumatology: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00144-2/fulltext
